Question: Will an ethical lawyer seek a Not Guilty verdict for a client he knows is guilty?
Answer: In the US criminal justice system, a conviction can and should be overturned if the defendant does not have a lawyer to represent him to a reasonable standard. If the lawyer representing the defendant doesn’t present a defense to a reasonable standard, then the conviction is overturned on the grounds of ineffective assistance of counsel. Ineffective assistance of counsel - Wikipedia A smart client who is guilty will tell his lawyer straight out that he did it. However, that does not change the ethical obligation of the lawyer to defend the defendants plea to the best of his ability. The defendant is asked how he pleas, guilty or not guilty. The lawyer may and should advise their client on how they should plea, but the decision on what plea to give is 100% the decision of the defendant. A recent case ruled on by the Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) was McCoy vs the state of Louisiana. McCoy was charged with capital murder and vehemently insisted on pleading not guilty. His lawyer, English however believed that the evidence of McCoy’s guilt was overwhelming and it would be unethical to not use the strategy of admitting guilt and trying and convince the jury in the penalty phase of the trial not to give McCoy the death penalty. English did not present any arguments that McCoy was not guilty or to try and discredit any of the evidence against McCoy. In fact with the judges approval, English told the jury during the guilt portion of the trial that McCoy was guilty. The jury convicted McCoy of the murder charges in the guilt phase, and despite his lawyer’s admission of guilt, the jury gave McCoy the death penalty. McCoy appealed the conviction on violation of US Constitution 6th Amendment right to counsel unsuccessfully to the Louisiana Supreme Court. McCoy then appealed to SCOTUS on the same grounds. SCOTUS ruled in McCoy’s favor stating: The Sixth Amendment guarantees a defendant the right to choose the objective of his defense and to insist that his counsel refrain from admitting guilt, even when counsel’s experienced-based view is that confessing guilt offers the defendant the best chance to avoid the death penalty. https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/17pdf/16-8255_i4ek.pdf SCOTUS overturned the trial court’s conviction and referred the case back to the trial court to retry. So it helped neither the defendant nor the state that the defense attorney did not argue to the best of his ability that his client was not guilty. It would take an incredible display of mental gymnastics to argue that the attorney’s actions were ethical. In fact, SCOTUS rulings tells us that it is unethical and illegal NOT to argue the client being not guilty to the best of the attorney’s ability if his client pleads not guilty. Now you may ask what would happen if there were no attorney’s willing to argue that the defendant was not guilty? Then the verdict would be overturned and likely have prejudice applied where the defendant would never be able to be tried for those crimes accused of. At the very least, no conviction could be upheld and millions of dollars would be spent in perpetually appealing an unsustainable verdict. A lawyer’s ethical obligation is to represent his client to the best of his ability without violating the law. The law requires the lawyer to argue that his client is not guilty even if the lawyer knows the client is guilty. Now the lawyer could not call a witness that the lawyer knew would give false testimony without informing the judge and prosecutor that the testimony was false. Depending on the state, the judge would decide on how to proceed. Someone falsely testifying in court is committing the crime of perjury. Question: Why would an innocent man not want people to testify in his behalf?
Answer: This question most clear addresses the right of the individual in the US not to be forced to nor penalized for not testifying against themselves as enshrined in the 5th Amendment to the US Constitution. And the most common reason that any defendant guilty or innocent would choose not to testify in his or her behalf is because doing so would also be testifying against herself or himself. Because anything you say can and will be used against you in a court of law. Often by a skilled prosecutor at twisting even the most innocent of statements into something sinister. Attorney’s routinely advise their clients not to testify in criminal proceedings because it can add little to no value to their case, which is establishing reasonable doubt to the charges by the state, but could likely be used by a skilled prosecutor to hurt their case. Often prosecutors will attempt to trick a defendant to making some reference to evidence deemed inadmissible by the judge, so that the prosecutor may now reference that evidence because the defendant referenced it. For example a prosecutor could attempt to get a defendant to reference a crime that the defendant was arrested, tried, convicted, and then exonerated for. This would most likely be disallowed by the judge for lack of relevance, but if the defendant brings it up, then it could become fair game. It would be highly prejudicial to many juries, but still present no direct proof of the crimes charged. I’ve seen a few awful answers by people claiming that an innocent man would not refuse to testify on his behalf. I implore those people to make sure that is explicitly told to both the judge and the defense attorney if ever you are called to be selected for a criminal trial. No one with this belief is capable of serving as an impartial juror in the US criminal justice system. I’ve seen several people take this to refer to Donald Trump’s impeachment. Neither the world nor the United States revolves around Donald Trump nor any other single individuals. We have tens of thousands of people being tried before juries in the US on criminal charges each year. This question goes involves a Constitutional right that goes far beyond whatever good or evil Donald Trump is ever to have been reasonably accused of. After Trump is dead there will still be hundreds of millions of US citizens that will depend on their right not to testify against themselves. Original Question: Why would an innocent man not want people to testify in his behalf?
